claim: In the Fang–Liu–Du information-dependent SIRM model, fix the positive demographic, transmission, recovery, baseline-vaccination and vaccine-efficacy parameters with \(R_0>1\). Let \(I^*\) be the unique endemic infected coordinate. Then \(I^*\) is strictly decreasing in the information-dependent vaccination coefficient \(u_0\) and the information growth rate \(a\), and strictly increasing in the saturation coefficient \(u_2\) and the information decay rate \(b\). Moreover, as \(u_0\to\infty\), one has \(I^*\to0\) and \(u_0 I^*\to Cb/(a\sigma)\), where \(C=(p_0\sigma+\mu)(R_0-1)\), while \(R_0\) itself is unchanged. Thus absence of \(u_0,u_2,a,b\) from \(R_0\) does not imply absence of an endemic-burden effect. For every finite positive parameter choice with \(R_0>1\), the endemic infected coordinate remains positive; no monotonicity claim is made for transient peaks, convergence rates, or global-attractor properties.
integrity: The motivating equilibrium equation, threshold formula, parameter meanings, numerical baseline, and source interpretation were checked against the public full text. The proof is analytic and the bundled computation is only a reproducibility check. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The accepted statement concerns the unique endemic equilibrium and exact parameter sensitivities. It does not establish transient-peak monotonicity, preservation of local or global stability under parameter changes, intervention cost-effectiveness, or finite-parameter eradication when \(R_0>1\). Related qualitative information-vaccination effects are known in other models.
title: Information-dependent vaccination shifts endemic burden at a fixed invasion threshold
